markdown: ## The two-minute brief - **The ECB is lining up a December hike.** Bundesbank President Nagel says a December rate rise is "very likely" to be necessary, and Kazimir and Radev are also pointing towards tighter policy [Reuters](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiqgFBVV95cUxNLXZ2Ull6Y3BwRjJpU1NOdnFIQWtNemRScG8yMzBZbmJSTk1zdHR3RUtwcUNRR0JaMEdSMmc1U0Fwdi1hYnBRX09KZmFiSTg4MGotV0I4Q0NPSlpEZVlMYnU1dzFBNjZ5VFJZN29ZQ2FGdnRjbHZDT3VGdnpCVFFBaUhscG1HMXV0UGUweEtmTUUyMVNGWVRWUnlocm1fSFlKWTU2ZHNhTGF2UQ?oc=5)[Breakingthenews.net](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMimwFBVV95cUxPdFFpZ3ZBTU9rVVZ0dkxacmpGZHMtZXB1ZmxncUNPQmlyN05BQUZicDVweVF5Sjd0WWJkOS1rWmk4cWN2TUVmbm5nRnlsWVljN1A1bWRVZkVLZGtPaG5MbGUtRm9UTnBaVzNudEVMMUZDckRpZ3ZSaFhaa1BKaE02cUpGTnlvcXRBZ3JGeUxLZDJ3MUNDYnpIbWNiQQ?oc=5)[investingLive](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMirgFBVV95cUxQS0dDZ3BVd055WFlkOTR0X1RlTF9aNUpYa0NnWDk4dDRFcmZIR3c0Y1hUQ1REZDBMbUd0cERDdVVzSXFhT3plYThXZ21vNTNKMENSaFJZb19HTFJ6eGpfT2g1YlNGc1NLYzNtaVA5X3BCamYxZUt1TkppdC1QUV9wU084VU9xckRFMmtRQTRGMUVmSXpWc2pKcUpVUWpSenpzeXJDLTFYV3VnRlhhbmc?oc=5)[Coin Edition](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMimgFBVV95cUxOVFJWejRvYnJFWTNteW9XbjB2NmNGMHZtYnpFNFh3RWZ1YzcyWE1XVUFpVW1RWFY4UmM0Y3ZNQzlhcUF1NzFhc09LWmw1aUtEbXI1YUlmZlFzSEtDT1Jua2ZMdU1aT2U0VHJmZlNPYWt3U29iRXR4THFpOHktUTBIU19PWURSYkxhdXh2UnNOWm9wRGRXN1lZNEFR?oc=5). Analysts see the deposit rate going from 2.5% to 2.75% [Yahoo Finance Singapore](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMid0FVX3lxTFBSanpZMVRtdDZTUkh0OHN6c2x4aFI2dXh2cEZ0WnctRTRXUF9ldWhDd3dCaEFSWVhOc3dfOFlzWXpWR0d5elVQMzdGdHVTS1FtWHE0cU1ZZXBaT1YzOHlBQzRhRklTc2cwMGVKcVN3MEdHNldXR1Vv?oc=5)[CEO Magazyn](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMigAFBVV95cUxNLThkblVNSWwyZVF4RWtaOHZoaXU0RVlDUGJqVFpTREE5bjUwd1RLMjFEbmpPVDNueE10SnVuVk1HMEJ3U1E0TVBxUVFSbGxobnIzVVluYU9EUW1Vc2F6RGJjbzBHNi1Qb2VoMVZQVXc5Tk1LVkVOaVdyNWstN1o2UQ?oc=5). *So what:* EUR funding costs and euro cash yields are heading higher, so revisit EUR hedge tenors and how deposits are laddered. - **Lagarde is leaving the ECB early, with inflation near double the target** [Yahoo Finance Singapore](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMid0FVX3lxTFBSanpZMVRtdDZTUkh0OHN6c2x4aFI2dXh2cEZ0WnctRTRXUF9ldWhDd3dCaEFSWVhOc3dfOFlzWXpWR0d5elVQMzdGdHVTS1FtWHE0cU1ZZXBaT1YzOHlBQzRhRklTc2cwMGVKcVN3MEdHNldXR1Vv?oc=5)[EU Perspectives](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiiwFBVV95cUxPN0stQ3lQY0RNaGNyRk1FUXo4YzBHdnBqVTFuNEx6Mm45eUU0RDB5V1NyeU5ueklSMTJKektOZXBCVnlCajlhTDNzX3ZpT3J3T3JoeXZCN2pQVUFfYk9XbXF5SUQ1TDZQdDktUklyNXFHS0dvUWhTLXVKZ0xLLXZPbUoyN2hmZ29HZ2dB?oc=5). *So what:* uncertainty over who leads the ECB adds to euro rate volatility just as the tightening cycle restarts. - **The EU and Canada plan to link their real-time payment systems** [Finextra](https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/48692/eu-and-canada-plan-to-link-real-time-payment-systems?utm_medium=rssfinextra&utm_source=finextrafeed). *So what:* this is a concrete step towards instant cross-border payments on a corridor relevant to North American manufacturers. - **Tokenised deposits settled cross-bank liquidity in real time in Hong Kong** [STT Info](https://news.google.?oc=5)[BigGo Finance](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMidkFVX3lxTFBZRl8wYXVDU2ZZN0tJLXZxVmJWUWNtX2xyTTJ1aWkwR1RvcG1jV0xwdDNvbDZWVXYzdHFHb1JISHN2XzdFaGlYMWcyNmRneGhTLUV3dEk0MGoyYXdwV2d1bTBKaDIyZ3pkbkxxQS1yQWZfM3o1enc?oc=5). *So what:* intraday liquidity and intercompany sweeps without cut-off times are moving from pilot towards production. - **Tariffs are still reshaping North American manufacturing.** Canadian manufacturing has contracted for the first time in 2026, while US manufacturing has grown for ten straight months [Investing.com](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiyAFBVV95cUxNZENnV2ZhckxOV1IxVEV5Z1JaSmVzRnJtSGpNMjlNVjhHYm9zQUF4N0hRT0ZWQlFFWlUtd1ctVWNHTE91RVNsTWVwMDYxeGVhWEtHcTF1MXpGLUdpYXFtWjBGZERpV3d0dnhva1piUXd1bnFHcnFaNFk2emlScnpXMHBYVlgzaGJyWlBtZW1fLV8xWUVnckZmMjZ2c2RkbzRHSFVkaU1OZEJpYTVhNUlUYjhKcFdxeW1hZThMQWlod0xLaTY1ZmlhYg?oc=5)[CFO Dive](https://www.cfodive.com/news/manufacturing-grows-10-straight-months-erratic-prices-dim-sentiment-inflation-gdp-economy/873500/). *So what:* plan for a gap between demand in the two markets, and for continued pressure on input costs. - **Trump has delayed robotics tariffs, and a Vietnam tariff decision is due by 29 November** [Legis1](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMifEFVX3lxTE5vdHM0Vk1FTlE4bG5lV1ZJM1RRUlVQWVNoSm9oaXc2SUo4cU9RZk9QTERFZHR6U2xRM09yV21saXo0ZXhtdTdpSE83eklUME1oTVZya05hQ1UwakJSZ1V2Zkd0cVRfWFJnUmdxVkI1NEhmTzViRGtGWTRhQnI?oc=5)[Cryptopolitan](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiekFVX3lxTE16ck16Q2N6NkxqSFNQOW1UWEk3Z3dWVTBPblRFekFYWTFvb1kxVmpxZVZiSHF2V0FYSnVmSWlkeF9xM2s0RHZqaU1JVnpwS2Nhb2ZtZ0h2RXZrWkFFQ2FGa3R6MlVzMjdyME1oRXRfRXBxcklRNUpOWmN3?oc=5). *So what:* the cost of automation capex has been reprieved for now, while supply-chain exposure to Vietnam remains an open question. ## Rates, FX & liquidity **USD.** Overnight funding is unchanged: SOFR is 3.95% and effective Fed Funds is 3.88%. The Treasury curve sold off modestly on the day, with the 2-year at 4.61% (+2bp) and the 10-year at 4.95% (+4bp). Over the week both are still lower (-9bp and -4bp), so the move steepened the curve. USD money-market yields near 4% still pay well on surplus cash, and term debt pricing near 5% on the 10-year argues for staying disciplined on duration when refinancing. **EUR.** €STR is unchanged at 2.441%, but the ECB rhetoric points to a 25bp rise in December [investingLive](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMirgFBVV95cUxQS0dDZ3BVd055WFlkOTR0X1RlTF9aNUpYa0NnWDk4dDRFcmZIR3c0Y1hUQ1REZDBMbUd0cERDdVVzSXFhT3plYThXZ21vNTNKMENSaFJZb19HTFJ6eGpfT2g1YlNGc1NLYzNtaVA5X3BCamYxZUt1TkppdC1QUV9wU084VU9xckRFMmtRQTRGMUVmSXpWc2pKcUpVUWpSenpzeXJDLTFYV3VnRlhhbmc?oc=5)[CEO Magazyn](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMigAFBVV95cUxNLThkblVNSWwyZVF4RWtaOHZoaXU0RVlDUGJqVFpTREE5bjUwd1RLMjFEbmpPVDNueE10SnVuVk1HMEJ3U1E0TVBxUVFSbGxobnIzVVluYU9EUW1Vc2F6RGJjbzBHNi1Qb2VoMVZQVXc5Tk1LVkVOaVdyNWstN1o2UQ?oc=5). Euro short-term investment yields should drift up, and the cost of carry on EUR/USD hedges will move with them. EUR/USD fell 0.33% on the day to 1.1179, though it is up 0.26% on the week, so the hawkish ECB commentary has not yet produced a sustained rally [The Portugal News](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMipwFBVV95cUxPeHZXR3JtUl9QbFRYZGVpdjFYWWYyX3A2Qms3NXUwYXcwdHdlRTJKX1ZuWHRsYzhlY1JKUGZnOGxZQkRwWi16dzZDcW1tMmk0OV9ubjQzOUVhaHYwVnpOM3d6bWk1ZmpVSFIzLUw3YUpja2p5a3VWUVRLX25aSk5pZWtUM1EwRWc2bkNsdjRZWGxGOHNrXy1yREthNkd1ZjlQc3dIQXJzUQ?oc=5). **GBP.** SONIA is 3.7348%. GBP/USD is 1.3411 (+0.62% over the week), and EUR/GBP has eased to 0.8336 (-0.36% over the week). Sterling is firming against the euro, which is relevant for EUR-GBP intercompany netting. **JPY, CNY, MXN.** USD/JPY is 158.29 (+0.25%), keeping the yen near weak levels, which makes JPY hedging cheap to carry but exposed to sharp reversals. USD/CNY rose 0.36% to 6.6723, a sizeable daily move for the renminbi. USD/MXN fell 0.66% to 18.597, so the peso strengthened, which raises the dollar cost of Mexican operating expenses. **Elsewhere.** Australia has raised rates for the fifth time this year, to the highest level since 2008 [FT Markets](https://www.ft.com/content/60283bdf-e45d-4723-a68e-5a857a5b949e?syn-25a6b1a6=1). This is a reminder that inflation pressure is still pushing some central banks to keep tightening. ## Treasury, cash & payments **EU and Canada commit to linking instant payment rails.** The two sides will connect their real-time payment systems and explore opening their markets to each other's banks and fintechs [Finextra](https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/48692/eu-and-canada-plan-to-link-real-time-payment-systems?utm_medium=rssfinextra&utm_source=finextrafeed). For a US manufacturer with Canadian and European entities, this could eventually cut the cost and float on intercompany and supplier payments. **Tokenised deposits deliver real-time cross-bank liquidity in Hong Kong.** Ant International and partner banks completed cross-bank liquidity management with tokenised deposits under the HKMA's Ensemble TX, with HKD settling in about five minutes [STT Info](https://news.google.?oc=5)[The Standard (HK)](https://news.google.?oc=5)[BigGo Finance](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMidkFVX3lxTFBZRl8wYXVDU2ZZN0tJLXZxVmJWUWNtX2xyTTJ1aWkwR1RvcG1jV0xwdDNvbDZWVXYzdHFHb1JISHN2XzdFaGlYMWcyNmRneGhTLUV3dEk0MGoyYXdwV2d1bTBKaDIyZ3pkbkxxQS1yQWZfM3o1enc?oc=5). This is worth tracking as a model for 24/7 pooling in Asia. **Bank of America expands cross-border real-time payments.** It cites growing client demand [Financial IT](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMisAFBVV95cUxORnVnVkVhTXcydXpQckRucmNsVjNpaHNrSXB4OGQzY0l1czZGSFI0eWQxdjV3MkxkUThOZXVNaGJOU0JoSW1WNnM4M0k1Y092ekpEbnU2czJJQnUxSVNSOWRuclJYd1pobjRzV2JiVGZoNjRFR2pYa2YxdVpCQjZTcGo5TEh2MElfcldRTjBSSTVGZXZqcWtTb3Nvd09Zd1BCLXN3RW5mZmxoeVFCQUdodA?oc=5). Ask relationship banks which corridors are live and how instant cross-border flows feed into cash-visibility reporting. **Banks are pushing AI-enabled, self-service exceptions handling.** Finextra pieces describe banks trying to close the corporate cross-border service gap and to give corporates control over payment exceptions [Finextra](https://www.finextra.com/event-info/645/cross-border-payments-how-banks-can-close-the-corporate-service-gap?utm_medium=rssfinextra&utm_source=finextrafeed)[Finextra](https://www.finextra.com/event-info/644/self-service-ai-enabled-payments-putting-corporates-in-control-of-exceptions?utm_medium=rssfinextra&utm_source=finextrafeed). These are useful prompts for the next bank service review. **Tokenised cash funds are gaining scale.** Spiko reports $2.38bn in its tokenised SAFO fund as business cash-management use grows [KuCoin](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMirwFBVV95cUxPNEg5YXNHakMxcVdrRmFkZVdST0dBX1BOelVFWlhmR0xlaVJ4LWs2bkhtZmRRdDlwQ2tzMTh4VTlGeHVhUm42THVJbC0tMmpNbS1Wa3cwanpUWllhc01ONEV1bVgxVVNadjI4VFMyb1dNb1JYTkdBa1g4cU9uMmZUVFRsQVZZNzBQRU9HRTlPdGhwcnlqTFlQdTN3WkNfLUlmY0VkY2x4OTdyNmUzY09j?oc=5). This sits at the edge of investment policy, but it shows where short-term investment products are heading. ## Banks, regulation & policy **Eurozone banks and insurers clash over the "Danish compromise".** Insurers argue that the rule, which makes it easier for Eurozone banks to own insurers, gives the banks an unfair advantage [FT Markets](https://www.ft.com/content/ab54dad5-f9d5-4e6c-b384-500410eb2082?syn-25a6b1a6=1). The outcome affects how much balance-sheet capacity bancassurance groups have. **The SEC eases audit quality-control rules.** The amended standards, which the Big Four endorsed, align with Chair Atkins' push to streamline compliance [CFO Dive](https://www.cfodive.com/news/sec-approves-easing-audit-quality-controls-endorsed-big-four-atkins-ey-pwc-deloitte-kpmg/873643/). Controllership and internal audit should note what changes in the external auditor's QC obligations. **Goldman bans AI coding tools for traders and bankers.** It cited productivity and risk concerns [Finextra](https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/48690/goldman-bans-traders-and-bankers-from-using-ai-coding-tools?utm_medium=rssfinextra&utm_source=finextrafeed). The move is relevant for any treasury team setting governance rules for AI-built scripts and models. **UK regulators float reforms for credit unions.** The PRA and FCA have put forward ideas to help the sector grow and innovate [Bank of England](https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/news/2026/november/regulators-explore-credit-union-reforms-to-support-growth-innovation-and-better-outcomes-for-members). ## Strategy, M&A & the industrial world **Tariffs bite in Canada while US factories keep growing.** Canadian manufacturing contracted for the first time this year as tariffs hit demand [Investing.com](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiyAFBVV95cUxNZENnV2ZhckxOV1IxVEV5Z1JaSmVzRnJtSGpNMjlNVjhHYm9zQUF4N0hRT0ZWQlFFWlUtd1ctVWNHTE91RVNsTWVwMDYxeGVhWEtHcTF1MXpGLUdpYXFtWjBGZERpV3d0dnhva1piUXd1bnFHcnFaNFk2emlScnpXMHBYVlgzaGJyWlBtZW1fLV8xWUVnckZmMjZ2c2RkbzRHSFVkaU1OZEJpYTVhNUlUYjhKcFdxeW1hZThMQWlod0xLaTY1ZmlhYg?oc=5)[Forex Factory](https://news.google.?oc=5). US manufacturing has grown for ten straight months, but erratic prices are weighing on sentiment, and one economist expects the AI-capex boom to support tech-related output rather than a broad manufacturing boom [CFO Dive](https://www.cfodive.com/news/manufacturing-grows-10-straight-months-erratic-prices-dim-sentiment-inflation-gdp-economy/873500/)[ing think](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMivwFBVV95cUxQRHlNMFlfbm40TDd6YVl4WmtXMDBjcTBkSS0xUjFveTdieTl6MFZkSmxCUzY1aGZyTXpGSnR3VzlvaERGYjFoQ3k1eWQ3b2NGOXl2ZHdFc19SQ292RWhGaWh4SXZRanhWT19CQmdCSkIyU0RUNDNMRlJrMDJjQTBHN242VHY0UmRxZlR0clAwQ09kRG1vSDBpLTAwbm5WMjU1NXFfTm9BdThCLXFwS2ZXZkJEcGJBQlR5WGF4Q19jWQ?oc=5). Experts describe tariffs as inflationary and disruptive to supply chains in both countries [BNN Bloomberg](https://news.google.?oc=5). **Trade policy shifts on robotics and Vietnam.** Trump has delayed robotics tariffs and ordered new trade negotiations [Legis1](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMifEFVX3lxTE5vdHM0Vk1FTlE4bG5lV1ZJM1RRUlVQWVNoSm9oaXc2SUo4cU9RZk9QTERFZHR6U2xRM09yV21saXo0ZXhtdTdpSE83eklUME1oTVZya05hQ1UwakJSZ1V2Zkd0cVRfWFJnUmdxVkI1NEhmTzViRGtGWTRhQnI?oc=5). Tesla and Samsung are opposing new US tariffs on Vietnam ahead of the 29 November deadline [Tekedia](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiqwFBVV95cUxOX3BDXzExQlFObk9qTzlocnpramk1eDlXVjVWSEVvLUU1NU4yOE9SSmN6NlhiUjdvVG9PcGFGSUVYTUJQdVhaUnpnQ2M4ZUFscnYwbDI2QjNuUEpxMm9uWXJ2NW9iUVF1SlVZcXliWlhoMzBYRTZ2dE81bnZ4SWlqUXc2QlZQT21QaXlvamtKbW5ScUxGM2VrbEE3WlBnXzNXRmVQYml2TVViN2s?oc=5)[Cryptopolitan](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiekFVX3lxTE16ck16Q2N6NkxqSFNQOW1UWEk3Z3dWVTBPblRFekFYWTFvb1kxVmpxZVZiSHF2V0FYSnVmSWlkeF9xM2s0RHZqaU1JVnpwS2Nhb2ZtZ0h2RXZrWkFFQ2FGa3R6MlVzMjdyME1oRXRfRXBxcklRNUpOWmN3?oc=5). Both decisions bear on automation budgets and sourcing. **Industrial bolt-on M&A continues.** Hexagon is buying Waygate to strengthen industrial inspection [Metrology and Quality News](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiogFBVV95cUxPZnNUTkJmTDF3ZlV0TGM0bVBGbE5CQ0RfbGdKZTZ6NDBFcWxONDBwdVRpXzRENGdvaVc0V1lGUjFQbTh2NUVUUzlfRjFFQTJCaDF0N2JBUUsyQm1SWm03OGo4NUJZeVhyRUVMTlh5S2xPM2pyak1XQU4wR2QwOWZCVGZQZUh5TjhYRE9uYjljTG1teGhTOFJ0d1ozeVRRQWlXanc?oc=5), Lonza is acquiring a Merck KGaA site to expand its US manufacturing footprint [Traders Union](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMipAFBVV95cUxPeTJjWTN2UzRHU20wVEQzamhNMU43MkI5RjdrU3FJRE5QdlREUXZtb0NRTHJlcXFEdXBUTGprN3pFYkxiZEI3dF9KbjBRWjhMbUhwR0FXUGNkSGJMV0tDakxxZGpLR3VHcmxkZXlVdzJZZ0xXWDVKaGdPVzFoSFZTMjhocmY4c1A2dUswVjBodTgtcEJGMHBkaHJ5ZjhBdEJLcWdObQ?oc=5), and Sopra Steria is taking Daher's industrial manufacturing engineering business [Pulse 2.0](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMixgFBVV95cUxPeHFlRl9hMEppZTQyckZFNmY5eUlTdm5iMVFlTmRYZ0hHS1VYc0pObW92NjhYaFpxNFpMR2RlUDJjbDJqWVlVM3BteE1kbk42c0hERHZNdFExOXcxNGpXYnRIMVY4LWdFNzZMWHhHZXJFQWh0Y0pDa005VjlmR2VYWnI2dzRncUE5anRtUmdxNmdoY21GbVAwZDBIMjBKNHJ3T2kwNWZYQ3JDYUVqY1hRdkgxT0xwbHBfRFB5WXgwNGI2TkdQSEE?oc=5). Buying onshore capacity remains a theme. **Working capital is weighing on industrial cash flow.** Huntsman's Q3 earnings improved, but working-capital outflows sharply weakened cash generation [TradingView](https://news.google.?oc=5). Commercial Vehicle Group restored profitability while cash flow stayed under pressure [TradingView](https://news.google.?oc=5). Celanese says 2027 cash generation hinges partly on working capital [TradingView](https://news.google.?oc=5). **Fiserv explores asset sales.** It has doubled its savings goal to $1bn and is talking to potential buyers [Payments Dive](https://www.paymentsdive.com/news/fiserv-talks-to-potential-asset-buyers/873604/). If you rely on Fiserv for processing, watch for changes in ownership or service. ## Worth thinking about The ECB is turning hawkish while US yields have edged lower on the week. If the December hike arrives and EUR/USD has not rallied, the rate gap that drives EUR forward points narrows, which changes the economics of hedging EUR receivables. A good question for the team is whether hedge tenors and euro cash placements are positioned for a 2.75% deposit rate [CEO Magazyn](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMigAFBVV95cUxNLThkblVNSWwyZVF4RWtaOHZoaXU0RVlDUGJqVFpTREE5bjUwd1RLMjFEbmpPVDNueE10SnVuVk1HMEJ3U1E0TVBxUVFSbGxobnIzVVluYU9EUW1Vc2F6RGJjbzBHNi1Qb2VoMVZQVXc5Tk1LVkVOaVdyNWstN1o2UQ?oc=5). At the same time, earnings across the industrial sector keep showing that working capital, not margin, is what hits cash conversion [TradingView](https://news.google.?oc=5)[TradingView](https://news.google.?oc=5)[TradingView](https://news.google.?oc=5). With tariff decisions on Vietnam and robotics pending [Legis1](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMifEFVX3lxTE5vdHM0Vk1FTlE4bG5lV1ZJM1RRUlVQWVNoSm9oaXc2SUo4cU9RZk9QTERFZHR6U2xRM09yV21saXo0ZXhtdTdpSE83eklUME1oTVZya05hQ1UwakJSZ1V2Zkd0cVRfWFJnUmdxVkI1NEhmTzViRGtGWTRhQnI?oc=5)[Cryptopolitan](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiekFVX3lxTE16ck16Q2N6NkxqSFNQOW1UWEk3Z3dWVTBPblRFekFYWTFvb1kxVmpxZVZiSHF2V0FYSnVmSWlkeF9xM2s0RHZqaU1JVnpwS2Nhb2ZtZ0h2RXZrWkFFQ2FGa3R6MlVzMjdyME1oRXRfRXBxcklRNUpOWmN3?oc=5), it is worth stress-testing inventory and supplier-payment terms. Supply chain finance capacity may matter more over the next two quarters than marginal yield on surplus cash.
